newsitem.title: UK: LME trade slow, as copper meanders around $2,200.
newsitem.headline: LME trade slow, as copper meanders around $2,200.

text.p: Business during Thursday's LME pre-market was slow, with market-leader copper fluctuating in a fairly tight band just above $2,200.
Other metals were also seeing little interest, and prices were similarly close to overnight levels, traders said.
"There isn't an awful lot going on in copper at the moment, but it should pick up again. The spreads are likely to remain lively, and they will drive the price," one said.
Copper touched $2,214 a tonne before settling back at $2,200, against Wednesday's close of $2,208. Cash/threes was at $160/179 backwardation.

Now that December options have been concluded, a lot of the recent uncertainty and liquidity has left the market. There is still the December "third Wednesday" pricing and tightness, although many positions have now been covered, they said.
Elsewhere, aluminium settled back to trade at $1,530, down $6 from Wednesday. The softer trend reflected copper, traders added.
Zinc held steady at $1,070, up $1, aided by recent mine closures, while lead was $1 higher at $689.
Nickel eased back under $6,900, lacking the drive to push up and re-test $7,000. Business was at $6,870, down $75.
Tin was just $5 adrift of overnight levels, trading at $6,110, while alloy was quoted at $1,365/70.
